skill-retro.why: Step 6 names ~/.claude/pr-review-recipes.md, this machine's measured how-tos that pr-review reads, among the local files kept out of the repo (+5 words)

pr-harden.why: State says that where CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG is on a live agent can outlast the gates' one-hour await bound, since its requests wait at a usage limit for the reset and the harness does not report it stalled (measured against a stub, artifacts/2026-10-21-retry-watchdog-limit), and that only the gate sees that hour pass, so its block past the bound opens on that await and the run records it again with the command that recorded it, --only and --run included, rather than re-dispatching its phase beside the live agent; once, an await naming one agent so that a name listed twice is that once spent, after which the agent is stopped with TaskStop before the dead-phase contract retries its phase; the rule moves here from resolve-ticket's Step 1 because resolve-ticket's alias reaches a standalone pr-harden or harden too

pr-harden/fixer.md.why: the header says that on a private PR the brief gives the fixer the key, nothing it commits names it or the ticket's URL, in the message, a comment, a test name or a changeSet id, the message describes what the code now does in its own words, and it runs the pre-push check before reporting its sha, so the sha the verifier runs is the one pushed; it rewrites rather than only amends, building again if that changed a file; and the brief gives it the PR's number to fetch with, keeping any message file outside the worktree, and reporting a squash a merge stops instead of looping on it

pr-harden/reviewer.md.why: the header says that on a private PR the brief gives the ticket's key, and that the PR's silence about the ticket, and a body without the loop's declines, is deliberate and not a finding

resolve-ticket/refuter.md.why: the plan refuter's seven questions, the JSON it returns and the rule every objection must meet move here from SKILL.md byte for byte, beneath a new header that tells it to read the file first and what its brief carries, the shape pr-harden 0.36.0 gave the fixer and the verifier, once role-file-check's wave 1 passed (2026-09-28). The header and SKILL.md's pointer are new text, so resolve-ticket grows by both, for a refuter that reads its questions as written

resolve-ticket.why: Step 1 pre-flights the usage limit beside the verifier: a claude.ai usage limit ends the turn with StopFailure hooks rather than Stop, so no gate sees it, while under CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG a request at the limit waits for the reset inside the turn (both measured against a stub, artifacts/2026-10-21-retry-watchdog-limit); so a run in a session pool-run does not carry itself, neither CLAUDE_PIPELINE_SESSION nor CLAUDE_PIPELINE_CARRY set, prints the variable and the running binary's version through CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH and, unless the variable is 1, true, yes or on in any case and the version reads 2.1.301 (Claude Code) or later, compared number by number, says so at once and carries on, giving the remedy for later sessions as Claude Code 2.1.301 or later started through a literal shell alias with a five-hour usage-limit wait cap, or for a pool-run --work session whose carry is off the same two variables before that command, never ~/.claude/settings.json's env, which the driver and a carried --work refuse to start under, and never a mid-run relaunch; and Step 7's await example records one await per agent, under its own name, so a name listed twice means what pr-harden's State takes it to

pr-review.why: Owner-directed final pass over all 722 review sessions (25 readers), 117 review memories and a fresh audit of the skill: a blocker checks the base and names its reach, severity being the refuter tallies' most common error; every fix recommended, prose included, goes to a refuter, broken or untested fixes being the next; agents start early, carry a budget in their brief and stop at 30 minutes, after 82 waits and a 16-hour unbounded refuter (def9cf70); probes count on the same terms as searches; runtime, consumer and privilege checks run where the code runs, P4 and P5 reopened by core PR 6462 (base 200, PR 500) and core PR 6694 (legacyui red); the private check runs first; CI that never ran a head is said and run; an exploitable defect the base already has goes to the user privately; addressing replies in its threads and, on the owner's own PR, fixes the description, because 0.34.0 took its 'own ask' boundary from a session's memory while the owner had asked for replies on legacyui PR 277 and fhir2 PR 635; the owner's own PR ends with an offer to apply and push, after 57 loops of the owner asking next; a recipes file, where it exists, holds this machine's how-tos; the round record is written mid-round with what a resumed session needs (c6f5028a); prunes, mostly the auditor's consolidation edits, remove about 290 words; per the readers' catalogs, 2026-11-19 (+456 words)

pr-review/posting.md.why: posting.md's gate fills its brackets each round and names the stacked PRs that merge first, after 47 sessions recited the bracket unfilled and 15 said 'not posted' after posting; the pre-post re-fetch covers every open PR in a stack, after six duplicate asks across one; posting waits for agents only up to their budget; per the readers' catalogs, 2026-11-19 (+51 words)

ticket-pool.why: the sentence listing what a ticket argument may be says a private ticket's JIRA key is never one and not to queue one, because the pool cannot tell it from a missing key, its headless sessions cannot read it, and its driver writes a record named for the key into the store skill-retro publishes

ticket-pool/pausing.md.why: the paragraph on which sessions the --work carry reaches says what carries a session started by hand besides Claude Code's own wait, CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG, which resolve-ticket's Step 1 says how to set; the driver's carry says Session drops that variable and its cap from every headless session, since one waiting under them neither ends nor goes quiet, the only two points at which the driver looks for a limit, and that the driver, and --work while its carry is on, refuse to start where ~/.claude/settings.json's env turns them on, a project's own settings unread; and the --work carry says that a session it carries starts without the pair, since one idle on a background agent waiting under it reads as stopped and would be nudged as if it were (reproduced with the real watch_hand_launched), and with CLAUDE_PIPELINE_CARRY=work, so that resolve-ticket's Step 1 does not warn, and that with the carry off resolve-ticket's Step 1 says what carries the session; and that --work passes crossSessionInbound: accept only while its carry is on, since at a limit_wait_max_seconds of 0 nothing sends the nudge it lets in

harden.why: Reporting says a /harden invoked on its own appends its run record, in pr-harden's format and file name with the branch, any / replaced by -, where the slice has no ticket or PR, since chartsearchai #435 (ten cycles) and querystore PR 100 (seven) reached a retro only through records written by hand; and Termination's bullets add that an edit rewriting a test owes the revert-check on the mutations that test caught before the edit, since in TRUNK-6826 and PR 100 a Phase 2 rewrite of a test changed what it could detect and a re-run mutation showed it

ticket-pool/by-hand.md.why: the paragraph on a --work session's environment no longer says nothing else is touched: while the launcher's carry is on, the session starts without CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG and its cap and with CLAUDE_PIPELINE_CARRY=work, which pausing.md explains, and while it is off without a CLAUDE_PIPELINE_CARRY it inherited, since the marker says the launcher carries the session
